correctness.rationale: For every κ_n, a crossing lands in (0,κ_n) or (-κ_n,0), the next n iterates keep that sign and cover the entire receiving half. Holding and switching-plus-recovery intervals give explicit nonzero-slope onto branches, so necessity and sufficiency hold for all finite words. Renewal recurrence gives entropy root; κ_n∼2^{-n} and root asymptotics yield the Lambert-W law. Standalone verification passed 12,276 finite words (diagnostics only).

originality.rationale: The 2019 Horan Markov sequence and adjacency matrices, the 2020 full-map spectral results, and the 2024 random-density/Oseledets study are credited as prior work. Their inspected statements do not explicitly establish the complete projected sign-switch language, its positive-measure sufficiency, or the factor-entropy collapse law. The different absolute-value factor does not cover sign switching. A prior equivalent projection is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The complete known state Markov adjacency graph might already have been projected and simplified elsewhere to the same sign-grammar entropy.
Exact sign shift is only the closure of sign-codable orbits; excluded hitting orbits cannot be represented by a binary sign at zero.
Search retrieval is not exhaustive; absence of a record is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Metastable residence signs are a natural measurement of the known two-half system. The theorem gives a complete sharp admissibility classification, not a generic rare-switch heuristic; it quantifies the loss of macroscopic information as leakage vanishes while local expansion remains strong. All n and all sign words are treated, with genuinely nontrivial sufficiency and a sharp entropy scale. The generic constrained-shift recurrence alone is not the claimed advance.
